newsitem.title: USA: Judge upholds strict state rules on oil tankers.
newsitem.headline: Judge upholds strict state rules on oil tankers.

text.p: A judge upheld Washington state regulations governing the operation of oil tankers even though they are stricter than federal laws.

U.S. District Judge John Coughenour on Monday dismissed a lawsuit filed by Intertanko, the International Association of Independent Tanker Owners, asserting the state regulations intended to prevent oil spills were superceded by federal laws governing marine traffic.
"The oil spill prevention laws legitimately protect Washington's delicate and valuable marine resources through the exercise of the state's police powers," Coughenour said in his 33-page opinion.
Jonathan Benner, a Washington lawyer representing Oslo, Norway-based Intertanko, said the trade group had not yet decided whether to appeal.

The state regulations, imposed in the wake of the 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill in Alaska, require tanker operators to file oil spill prevention plans to describe their compliance with testing, inspection and lookout practices beyond what is required by federal law. Tankers operating in Washington state waters also must be equipped with an emergency towing system.
Intertanko contended the regulations were unconstitutional because they regulated interstate commerce and were contradicted by coastal regulations.
"The thrust of our complaint is that the state shouldn't be operating in these areas," Benner said.
But Coughenour said Congress specifically made provisions for states to impose tougher tanker laws if they desired.

The costs of complying with the state regulations were estimated at $12,000 for each plan filed by an independent operator and $80,000 to equip each tanker with a towing system, compared with up to $19 million to operate a tanker for a year.
"Given the relatively minimal cost of compliance as compared to the costs of an oil spill, Intertanko cannot demonstrate that the incidental burdens ... are clearly excessive," Coughenour said.
